chapter.title: Standard Streams
chapter.para: When Python creates an interpreter, Rexx's standard streams go through Python's, as BSF4ooRexx sends them through Java's: SAY, trace output, error messages, .output~lineout and everything else written to .output, .error and .traceOutput reaches sys.stdout and sys.stderr, and PULL and LINEIN read sys.stdin. The Python streams are looked up at every call, so Rexx's output is seen in Jupyter, or wherever Python sends its own (contextlib.redirect_stdout). oorexx.Interpreter(stdio=False) keeps Rexx's own streams.

Each line carries BSF4ooRexx's prefix, so that Rexx's lines stand out in a log or a notebook: REXXout>, REXXerr>, REXXtrc>, and, as the prompt before reading, REXXin?> and REXXdbgIn?>. prefixes=False leaves them out; a dict gives the prefixes of the streams it names ("input", "output", "error", "debuginput", "traceoutput"), and the others have none. From Rexx, .output~current~prefix = .nil removes one. Each line is a single write, so lines from several threads do not mix.

example.title: Rexx's output through Python's
example.programlisting:
import io, contextlib, oorexx
with oorexx.Interpreter() as rexx: rexx.routine("say 'hello'")() buffer = io.StringIO() with contextlib.redirect_stdout(buffer): rexx.routine("say 'captured'")() print(repr(buffer.getvalue())) with oorexx.Interpreter(prefixes={"output": "rexx> "}) as rexx: rexx.routine("say 'custom'")() with oorexx.Interpreter(prefixes=False) as rexx: rexx.routine("say 'plain'")()

chapter.para: A program started by rexx keeps Rexx's streams, and can send them to Python's with call py.redirectTo (), and back with call py.redirectTo "R".

example.title: py.redirectTo
example.programlisting:
say "Rexx's own" call py.redirectTo say "through Python's sys.stdout" .output~current~prefix = .nil say "without the prefix" call py.redirectTo "R" say "Rexx's own again"
::requires "python.cls"
example.screen: Rexx's own REXXout>through Python's sys.stdout without the prefix Rexx's own again

section.title: PyOutputStream Class
section.para: A subclass of Rexx's OutputStream that writes to a Python text stream, with the methods of BSF4ooRexx's BSF.OutputStream. The stream is the name of one of the streams of Python's sys ("stdout", "stderr"), looked up at every write, or a Python file object. Each line starts with the prefix, also after every line feed inside it. Its methods are unguarded.

section.title: new (Class Method)
section.para: Returns a stream that writes to stream (default "stdout"), with prefix (default &nil;, none).

section.title: arrayOut
section.para: Writes each item of array as a line. Returns 0.

section.title: charOut
section.para: Writes string, without a line end. The prefix goes before it if it starts a line. Returns 0.

section.title: close
section.para: Does nothing, and returns 0: the Python stream stays open.

section.title: file
section.para: Returns the Python stream it writes to now (for a name, the current sys stream), or &nil; when it is &None; (as sys.stdout is under pythonw).

section.title: lineOut
section.para: Writes line (default empty) and a line end, in one write. Returns 0.

section.title: prefix
section.para: Returns the prefix, or &nil; for none.

section.title: prefix=
section.para: Sets the prefix; &nil; for none.

section.title: say
section.para: The same as .

section.title: stream
section.para: Returns the stream given to new: a name, or a Python file object.

section.title: string
section.para: Returns a description: a PyOutputStream (stdout, prefix REXXout>).

section.title: PyInputStream Class
section.para: A subclass of Rexx's InputStream that reads a Python text stream, with the methods of BSF4ooRexx's BSF.InputStream: "stdin", looked up at every read, or a Python file object. Before reading a line, it writes its prefix to .output as a prompt. Its methods are unguarded.

section.title: new (Class Method)
section.para: Returns a stream that reads stream (default "stdin"), with prefix (default &nil;, none) as its prompt.

section.title: arrayIn
section.para: Returns a Rexx Array of the remaining lines, without their line ends.

section.title: charIn
section.para: Returns the next length characters (default 1); start is ignored, as a Python stream is read in order. Returns an empty string at the end.

section.title: chars
section.para: Returns 1: a Python stream cannot tell how much is left, so it answers as a terminal does.

section.title: close
section.para: Does nothing, and returns 0.

section.title: file
section.para: Returns the Python stream it reads now, or &nil; when it is &None;.

section.title: lineIn
section.para: Writes the prefix to .output, as a prompt, then reads a line and returns it without its line end. Returns an empty string at the end.

section.title: lines
section.para: Returns 1, as .

section.title: prefix
section.para: Returns the prefix, or &nil; for none.

section.title: prefix=
section.para: Sets the prefix; &nil; for none.

section.title: stream
section.para: Returns the stream given to new.

section.title: string
section.para: Returns a description: a PyInputStream (stdin, prefix REXXin?>).
